facts.claim: Microplastics were not biomagnified in the edible parts of the marine food web of the Persian Gulf; instead, trophic dilution occurs.
facts.quote: the results of the trophic magnification factor (TMF) and biomagnification factor (BMF) calculation indicated that MPs were not biomagnified in edible parts of the marine food web of the Persian Gulf.

facts.claim: Microplastic concentrations in human liver and brain samples increased over time between 2016 and 2024.
facts.quote: the time of death (2016 versus 2024) was a significant factor, with increasing MNP concentrations over time in both liver and brain samples (P = 0. 01).

facts.claim: Greater accumulation of nanoplastics was observed in human brains with a documented dementia diagnosis, specifically in cerebrovascular walls and immune cells.
facts.quote: even greater accumulation of MNPs was observed in a cohort of decedent brains with documented dementia diagnosis, with notable deposition in cerebrovascular walls and immune cells.

facts.claim: No clear sign of microplastic biomagnification in situ was observed at the higher trophic levels.
facts.quote: Combined, these findings indicate that, although bioaccumulation of MPs occurs within trophic levels, no clear sign of MP biomagnification in situ was observed at the higher trophic levels.

facts.claim: Microplastics were found in human brain tissues, with higher proportions of polyethylene than in the liver or kidney.
facts.quote: Brain tissues harbor higher proportions of polyethylene compared to the composition of the plastics in liver or kidney

facts.claim: Studies have confirmed that nano- and microplastics can induce apoptosis in cells and have genotoxic and cytotoxic effects.
facts.quote: Most studies to date have confirmed that nano- and microplastics can induce apoptosis in cells and have genotoxic and cytotoxic effects.

research.angle: While microplastics are found in human tissues and linked to dementia, evidence suggests they may dilute rather than biomagnify as they move up the food chain.
research.verdict: The sources confirm that microplastics and nanoplastics are present in human tissues and can cause cellular damage, but they do not consistently show biomagnification in marine food webs.
research.caveat: Many studies lack sufficient data to evaluate specific human health effects or the pathways of exposure and clearance.
